details: DRISHYAM 1.1  COMPLAINANT: Mahesh Deshmukh, r/o Panjim, Goa.  MISSING PERSON: Sameer "Sam" Deshmukh, age 19, male.  INCIDENT DETAILS: Subject has been unreachable since the evening of October 2. Subject's yellow imported car is also missing. Last known location was near Pondolem village, Goa. Subject's mother, IGP Meera Deshmukh, noted his phone has been switched off since 23:45 HRS on Oct 2. Subject was supposed to attend a nature camp.  INITIAL ACTION: Wireless message flashed across all checkposts in North and South Goa. Local stations instructed to look out for the yellow vehicle. Sub-Inspector Laxmikant Gaitonde assigned to preliminary local inquiry in Pondolem. Salgaonkar (Logged into office PC)  ENTRY 01: Searched the quarry site based on a tip. Found the yellow car belonging to the missing person sunk in the deep water. Suspect foul play. ENTRY 02: Interrogated Vijay Salgaonkar and his family (Nandini, Anju, Anu). Suspect them due to past enmity between Vijay and myself, and local rumors.  ENTRY 03: Vijay claims his family was in Panjim on Oct 2 and Oct 3. They state they attended Swami Chinmayananda's Maha Satsang on Oct 2, stayed at a lodge, ate Pav Bhaji at Martin's Corner (Wait, Ashok Restaurant), and watched a movie on Oct 3.  ENTRY 04: Cross-verified alibi. Bus conductor confirms they traveled on Oct 2. Lodge manager confirms booking. Swami's CD shows them in the crowd. Restaurant owner remembers Vijay describing the Pav Bhaji. Movie theater clerk confirms ticket purchase. The alibi is completely airtight. ENTRY 05: Note to self - It feels too perfect. Usually, people forget small details. The entire family is repeating the exact same sequence of events, like a script.  ENTRY 06: Recovered Sam's phone from a truck carrying sand to a different state. Driver claims someone threw it into the back of his truck while it was parked near the highway. Driver described a middle-aged man arriving in a yellow car matching the missing vehicle. ENTRY 07: Investigated the new Panjim Police Station construction site. The contractor noted Vijay Salgaonkar visited the site alone early morning on Oct 3 to "inspect cable wiring requirements," though no official contract was awarded. Height matches V. Salgaonkar, but inconclusive.  WITNESS: Martin (Diner Owner, Pondolem) STATEMENT: "Yes, I know Vijay. He runs the Mirage Cable network. Was he here on the 2nd? No, I don't think so. Wait, actually, he told me yesterday that he was in Panjim on the 2nd for the Satsang. If he says he was there, he must have been."  WITNESS: Swami Chinmayananda Satsang Organizer STATEMENT: "We had thousands of devotees on October 2nd. I cannot verify every face. But the police showed me a video recording from the event. You can see Mr. Salgaonkar and his family standing in the back row for about five seconds."  WITNESS: Bus Conductor (Route: Pondolem to Panjim) STATEMENT: "I punch hundreds of tickets a day. I remember Vijay because he argued with me about the change on October 2nd. He gave me a 500 rupee note for tickets that cost 120."  WITNESS: Night Watchman (Highway Toll Naka) STATEMENT: "Around 4 AM on the 3rd, I saw that yellow imported car heading towards the quarry. There was only one person inside. It looked like the cable guy, Vijay. I remember because he usually drives a scooter, not a fancy car."
